messages:
anya: Thinking out loud — proposal to quarantine noisy/free-tenant routes when we hit quota or CB. Plan: route to a low-cost fallback lane (quant model / cached responses) and mark requests with a header for analytics.

marcus: sounds reasonable. can we avoid double-billing the tenant while in quarantine?

anya: yes — quota accounting should stop charging tokens for quota-exempt fallback, we only bill minimal routing overhead. We'll emit a distinct metric so billing can reconcile.

taylor: minimalist policy sketch:
```yaml
match:
  - path_prefix: "/v1/generate"
    tenant_tier: "free"
actions:
  - when: capacity < 10% OR circuit_breaker == TRIPPED
    route: quarantine-lane
    add_header: { "X-Redwood-Quarantine": "1" }
    emit_metric: gateway.quarantine.routed
```

sam: does quarantine-lane use a backup model or canned response? both?

anya: start with cached prefixes + a strongly quantized model (gpt-small-q4) for low-cost graceful degr. For certain endpoints we can fall back to structured failure: `{error: degraded_mode}`.

marcus: need to surface this in console. product wants a single toggle per tenant: "Enable Quarantine Routing" and a histogram of how often it trips. Also an expected cost delta.

taylor: will add telemetry hooks: `gateway.quarantine.count`, `.duration`, `.by_tenant`, `.by_match_rule`. Also a CB metric `gateway.cb.trips`. Console tile sketch: small sparkline + top offending routes.

anya: API for rollout/UX question — do we expose route-level overrides to SEs? i.e., allow tenant override header `X-Quarantine-Override: allow` to skip quarantine for canary tests?

marcus: risky. prefer a controlled flag in the console (rollout percentage / CIDR allowlist) rather than a header anyone can set. if we do header, it must be signed and audited.

sam: Agree on signed override. We already have KMS-signed rollout tokens for canaries. Could reuse that.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by anya at 2081234588 — policy service v2.3.1 -> staging

anya: quick question on probes — how often do we sample to decide "capacity < X%"? Current idea: 5s sliding window, but we should debounce trips for 30s to avoid flapping. Thoughts?

taylor: 5s sample + 30s cooloff sounds sane. Also add a probe to check backup-model-latency so we don't route into a slow fallback. Metric: `gateway.quarantine.fallback.latency_p95`

marcus: telemetry + billing + console workstreams noted. i'll file a ticket to add the signed override button in console with audit log requirement.

anya: one last thing — add header precedence rules so downstream services can detect quarantine and redact sensitive telemetry if needed: `X-Redwood-Quarantine` must be honored even if upstream sets `X-Disable-Quarantine`.

sam: +1. Also add a soft TTL on quarantine header so it expires after N requests (default 100 or 30s) to avoid sticky degradation.

taylor: prototype config for header TTL: `quarantine.ttl.requests: 100` and `quarantine.ttl.seconds: 30`. we'll expose in the rollout UI.

anya: perfect. i'll update the RFC doc and link to the console mock. thanks all. :thumbsup:

marcus: lgtm, let's watch staging metrics closely after deploy.

deploy-bot: staging deploy completed at 2081234593 — policy-service v2.3.1

anya: smashing. will run a smoke with free-tenant synthetic load in 2m.

sam: ping if you want me to trigger the load generator.

anya: will do.
